title: QBR Metric Anchor and Measurement Fabric
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a lightweight living doc for QBR presenters and CS analysts that standardizes the core metric definitions we use when talking to customers about performance, cost, and renewal health. Focused on the four signal families we look at most during account reviews: latency, uptime/availability, cost-per-token, and cache hit rate.

Audience:
- CSMs preparing QBRs
- CS analysts creating renewal trackers
- Solutions & SEs working on performance remediation

How to use this doc:
- Use the KPI table below as the canonical mapping for dashboards and slide snippets.
- If you deviate from these definitions for a given customer, note the override and why.

Metric definitions (canonical):
1) Latency (request-level generation latency)
- Definition: time from request received to first-byte (streaming) or final-token emitted, per inference request.
- Reported buckets: p50, p90, p95, p99, median token time when relevant.
- Measurement window: 30d rolling for trend, 7d for QBR snapshot.
- Notes: break out by model variant, sequence-length bucket (short <64, medium 64–512, long >512), and route. Exclude obvious synthetic tests and health-check probes.
- Common pitfalls: mixing token-level latency (per-token generation) with end-to-end request latency (includes network & pre/post-processing). Always label which you report.

2) Uptime / Availability
- Definition: percent of requests that received a successful 2xx response within SLO threshold (service-level latency cap — normally 10s for API customers).
- Calculation: (successful_requests_within_SLO) / (total_valid_requests) over window.
- Reporting cadence: 30d and 365d for contract-level conversations.
- Dependencies: include downstream infra incidents (region-level) and scheduled maintenance; flag any customer-impacting failovers.

3) Cost per token (unit economics)
- Definition: end-to-end cost allocated to customer requests divided by produced tokens. Includes: compute amortized (GPU hours apportioned), storage/cache cost (small), data-transfer and platform overhead. Does NOT include third-party model licensing fees when billed separately.
- Reporting: $/k token (thousand tokens) and $/1k prompt tokens + $/1k completion tokens where available.
- Measurement notes: use normalized tokenization (common BPE measure); if customer uses a non-standard tokenizer note correction. Show both raw and cache-adjusted numbers (see cache hit rate).

4) Cache hit rate (prefix + KV cache)
- Definition: percentage of requests where at least X% of tokens were served from cache (for our purposes X=50% as a quick threshold) OR a cached KV lookup satisfied the retrieval.
- Report both: prefix-cache-hit-rate (front-loaded prompts) and kv-cache-hit-rate (internal model KV reuse).
- Measurement window: 7d rolling for operational troubleshooting, 30d for QBR narrative.
- Impact: translate hit-rate into tokens saved and show estimated $ savings in cost table.

Suggested KPI table (canonical columns):
- metric_name | definition_summary | primary_dashboard | reporting_window | owner | target | action_if_breached
- Example rows (CSV-style):
"latency_p95","Request p95 end-to-end (incl pre/post)","dashboards/cs/latency","30d","eng-sre","<400ms (short requests) / <800ms (medium)","investigate batch sizes, routing, quantization profile"
"availability_30d","% requests within 10s SLO","dashboards/cs/availability","30d","product-hosted-api",">=99.5%","run incident RCA, enable fallback routing"
"cost_per_1k_tokens","Platform cost allocated per 1k produced tokens (cache adjusted)","dashboards/finance/costs","30d","finance-ops","<$0.80 for baseline models","recommend batching, enable cache, review model sizing"
"cache_effective_hit","% requests with >=50% tokens served from cache","dashboards/cs/cache","30d","eng-serving-runtime",">30%","review cache TTLs, prefixing patterns, customer prompt engineering"

Data sources & sampling guidance:
- Source of truth should be our metrics pipeline (prod metrics), not client-side instrumentation. For ad-hoc verification use logs/trace samples.
- Sampling: for p95/p99 use 1% stratified sample across routes to speed queries; validate sample stability monthly.
- Timezones: normalize to customer region or UTC (note what you chose in slides).

Recommended query snippets (pseudocode):
- p95 latency: SELECT percentile(95, end_to_end_ms) FROM requests WHERE model=XX AND created_at BETWEEN X AND Y AND not synthetic
- cache-hit rate: SELECT count_if(cache_fraction>=0.5)/count(*) FROM requests WHERE model=XX AND created_at BETWEEN X AND Y
- cost per token: total_allocated_cost/total_generated_tokens (show raw and cache-adjusted)

Communicating changes and overrides:
- If you change the measurement window (e.g., 90-day vs 30-day) or the hit threshold for cache, add a short note in the QBR appendix: "Metric override: latency p95 uses 90d because customer traffic is highly seasonal."
- Keep a one-line rationale when converting metrics into business impact (e.g., "$0.25/token saved = 18% cost reduction vs baseline")

Quick presenter checklist (for each QBR slide):
- Did I label whether latency is token-level or request-level?
- Did I include model name and sequence-length buckets?
- Did I show cost both raw and cache-adjusted?
- Do I have owner & next steps for any metric flagged amber/red?

Unresolved questions / items to refine:
- Standardized method for attributing multi-tenant GPU amortization to customers (finance request).
- Define a canonical cache-hit threshold for all customers (proposal: 50% for QBR, but some teams want 20%).

Appendix (short examples to copy into slides):
- "In the last 30 days p95 latency for your primary route (model-x, seq<64) is 420ms (target 350ms). The top contributor is long-tail sequences; recommended action: apply request routing to medium-length optimized model and enable aggressive prefix caching for prompts > 128 tokens."
- "Cache-adjusted cost per 1k tokens: $0.62 (raw $0.93). Current cache hit is 36% which corresponds to ~$0.31 saved per 1k tokens versus running cold."

Notes to self (CS analyst):
- Keep a short changelog here when you tweak thresholds.
- When in doubt, prefer conservative (higher) latency numbers for customer-facing docs and show internal optimistic numbers in a separate slide.

End of doc.
